items.subject: english
items.title: adiaphoron
items.text: a religious ceremonial or ritual observance that is held to be an affair of the individual conscience because it is neither forbidden nor enjoined by the scriptures.; (Stoic philosophy) a matter having no moral merit or demerit.

englishDefinitions: a religious ceremonial or ritual observance that is held to be an affair of the individual conscience because it is neither forbidden nor enjoined by the scriptures.
(Stoic philosophy) a matter having no moral merit or demerit.
englishExamples: For all of the wild-eyed (and completely sectarian) assertions floating around the LCMS that ordination is a mere adiaphoron, that ‘laying on of hands’ does not mean ritual ordination but rather a democratic election, that ordination confers nothing - I have yet to ever read about anyone actually graduating seminary and taking a call to a congregation and choosing to forgo the rite of ordination.

Esteem (or reputation, fame, glory) was for Stoics an adiaphoron, and though it could be classed as prolegomenon with a certain ‘value’, it was only after Diogenes' time that they conceded that its ‘value’ was more than instrumental.
